title: Records, nullable values and dictionaries
prompt: Book is supplied. Its Author may be null. Write two methods. public static Book Renamed(Book book, string title) returns a copy with the new title and the same Id and Author. public static Dictionary<string, int> CountByAuthor(List<Book> books) returns the number of books for each author. Books whose Author is null are counted under the key "Unknown". An empty string is a real author name and gets its own key.
hints: Which author values are there to tell apart: a name, an empty string, and what else?
Turn a null author into the key "Unknown" before you touch the dictionary. Leave an empty string as it is.
Use book with { Title = title } for the copy. For the counts, use book.Author ?? "Unknown" as the key and add 1, starting a new key at 1.
checks: Practice.Renamed(new Book(2, "Emma", null), "Send") == new Book(2, "Send", null)
checkLabels: Renamed must change the title and keep the Id and Author.
Renamed must keep a missing Author missing.
The 2 books with no author must be counted under "Unknown".
An empty author name is its own key, with 1 book.
The board must give exactly three keys.
An empty list must give an empty dictionary.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Treats an empty author name as a missing author.
Uses a missing author directly as a dictionary key.

feedback: Look at how a null author, an empty author name and a real name are each turned into a key. They must give three different keys.
